modules.title: Proportion
modules.summary: A proportion is an equality between two ratios. Cross multiplication is used to test and solve proportions.

questions.text: Which topic belongs to Proportion?
Complete a key rule: a/b = c/d
A proportion is an equality between two ratios. Cross multiplication is used to test and solve proportions.
Solve the proportion 5/8 = x/24.
Write one key concept from this lesson.
Solve 4/5 = x/20.
Are 6/8 and 9/12 proportional?
Find x if 3:x = 6:14.

modules.title: Applications of Ratio and Proportion — Scale Drawings
modules.summary: Scale drawings compare a length in a drawing or model with the real length after using the same units.
examples: 1 : 500,000 means 1 cm on the map represents 5 km in reality.

Write one key concept from this lesson.
questions.answer: scale drawing / drawing length / real length

questions.text: A map scale is 1:100000. What real distance does 3 cm represent in km?
Drawing length is 5 cm and real length is 250 cm. Write the scale in simplest form.

modules.title: Applications of Ratio and Proportion — Proportional Division
modules.summary: Proportional division splits money, land, profit, or another quantity into shares according to a given ratio.
formulas: one part = total / sum of ratio parts
share = one part × its ratio number

questions.text: Which topic belongs to Applications of Ratio and Proportion — Proportional Division?

questions.answer: one part = total / sum of ratio parts

modules.title: Applications of Ratio and Proportion — Percentages
modules.summary: Percentages express a part out of one hundred and are used in discounts, increases, decreases, profit, and everyday problems.

modules.title: Mathematical Expressions and Formulas / Algebraic Terms
modules.summary: Algebraic expressions use variables, constants, coefficients, and operations. Formulas express relationships between quantities.
examples: In 5x+3, 5 is the coefficient and 3 is the constant.

modules.title: Parallelism
modules.summary: When a transversal cuts parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal and interior angles on the same side are supplementary.
examples: A corresponding angle to 65° is also 65°.

examples: Every square is a rectangle and a rhombus.
